notes: ACCESS: robots.txt fetched FIRST at https://jysk.dk/robots.txt (HTTP 200, curl_cffi safari17_2_ios). Full contents: 'User-agent: *  / Disallow: /customer/  / Disallow: /checkout/  / Disallow: /b2b/  / Disallow: *filters=*  / Disallow: *sort=*  / Disallow: /search  / Sitemap: https://jysk.dk/sitemap.xml'. There is NO group naming ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, Claude-Web or Claude - the file has exactly one group. No Crawl-delay. I honoured the facet ban strictly: every URL requested is a bare category path with no filters= or sort= parameter, I never touched /search, /customer/, /checkout/ or /b2b/, and I did not use JYSK's internal search endpoint even though the PLP toolbar exposes one. The sitemap is on the same host, so no second-host robots check was needed. All requests returned HTTP 200 via probe.fetch(); no bot wall. TREE: JYSK runs a headless Next.js storefront whose mega-menu is client-loaded, so the homepage HTML exposes only the ten top-level nodes (/badevaerelse, /sovevaerelse, /stue, /spisestue, /kontor, /opbevaring, /gardiner, /have, /indretning, /entre). The Badeværelse landing page itself lists only 6 children - which would have TRUNCATED the branch. I recovered the complete tree from JYSK's OWN robots-declared sitemap (https://jysk.dk/sitemap.xml, 6,062 URLs) by taking every path that is a proper prefix of another path, which yields 281 real category nodes. That recovered the entire third level that the landing page hides: Badeforhængsstænger under Badeforhæng, all EIGHT children of Badeværelsestilbehør (Diverse, Duftpinde, Håndklædeholdere, Opbevaring til badeværelse, Sæbedispensere, Tandbørsteholdere, Toiletbørster, Toiletspande) and the three children of Håndklæder. The 8-child list was independently confirmed on-page: every Badeværelsestilbehør leaf renders its full sibling list in its own left-nav. Breadcrumb checked on the leaves (e.g. Forside / Badeværelse / Badeværelsestilbehør / Sæbedispensere). QTY: every JYSK listing renders its own exact total in plain text immediately above the grid as 'N varer' (N items), and the grid is SERVER-RENDERED in full - there is no pagination and no client fetch. I proved the figure independently on every node by counting the distinct product-detail URLs present in the delivered HTML under that category path: 21 varer = 21 product URLs (Sæbedispensere), 45=45 (Bademåtter), 43=43 (Diverse), 25=25 (Opbevaring), 14=14 (Tandbørsteholdere, Toiletbørster, Børnehåndklæder, Hjemmesko), 13=13 (Toiletspande), 12=12 (Badeforhængsstænger, Vaskeklude), 10=10 (Håndklædeholdere), 17=17 (Badekåber), 15=15 (Duftpinde), 11=11 (Vasketøjskurve), 25=25 (Spejle), 1=1 (Strandhåndklæder). Exact match on all 17 leaf pages, which proves 'N varer' is the true total and not a page size. No estimate, no API, no JSON-LD numberOfItems (JYSK does not emit one, and it would have capped at 100 anyway). PARENT ROLL-UP TRAP FOUND AND AVOIDED: JYSK parents show a total that INCLUDES their children's products. Badeforhæng shows 24 = its own 12 curtains + the 12 rod/ring products of its child. Badeværelsestilbehør shows 155 = 21+14+13+14+43+15+10+25 exactly. Håndklæder shows 91 = 64 own + 14 + 1 + 12. Those three are therefore treated as grouping/roll-up nodes and never recorded as leaves (rules 24/26, no aggregation). The top node /badevaerelse renders no count at all - it is a landing page with no grid - and is the top grouping row. VERIFICATION: recorded counts discriminate (12/21/14/13/14/43/25/10 - seven distinct values, no site constant). H1 checked on every page and matches the node ('Sæbedispenser til enhver stil', 'Praktiske toiletspande og pedalspande', 'Opbevaring til badet, bruseren og badeværelset'). rel=canonical checked on every node and every one is self-canonical to the exact clean URL recorded - no canonical-alias blind spot, so the dedup misses below are trustworthy. DEDUP: lib/dedup.already_extracted() run on all 19 candidates. All eight recorded leaves MISS, including the OPTION-1 risk node /badevaerelse/badevaerelsestilbehor/opbevaring-til-badevaerelse (bathroom shelves, shower caddies, hanging storage) - it is NOT in Furniture.xlsx, so it correctly comes into Bathroom. The one HIT in the sweep is /indretning/spejle -> Final.xlsx (Home Decor pass) 'Mirrors', which is why the mirror node is in review and not in rows. The index holds 60+ other jysk.dk URLs from Furniture.xlsx and Final.xlsx, confirming the matcher fires on this domain. EXCLUDED: Duftpinde routed to DECOR; Badeforhæng, Badekåber, Bademåtter and Håndklæder (+3 children) routed to TEXTILE; Hjemmesko excluded as footwear; Vasketøjskurve excluded as a Vask-og-stryg (laundry) node; Spejle excluded as already extracted. The recorded 'Diverse' leaf was inspected product-by-product before inclusion: it is JYSK's genuine catch-all bathroom-accessory node (bathroom shelf BENSBYN, toilet roll holders SUNDSBRUK/TRARYD/VANSBRO, bathroom scale VENJAN, squeegees DJURA/FORSBY, bath brush VALJE, double-sided mirror ILSBO, LED makeup mirror VEDDIGE, storage jars, trinket dishes) - primary function bathroom accessories, so it stays in Bathroom; note it contains one lighting SKU ('Makeup lampe med LED KALIX') which is a single product, not a node, and does not change the node's classification. FINALLY: JYSK Denmark sells NO sanitaryware - no baths, showers, enclosures, screens, taps, WCs, basins, bidets or vanity units. Confirmed against the full 281-node sitemap-derived category tree, which contains no such node anywhere. That absence is verified, not assumed.
